claims.explanation: Repaglinide is a meglitinide insulin secretagogue that closes ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channels by binding the SUR1/Kir6.2 complex (ABCC8/KCNJ11), and it also inhibits mitochondrial respiration and induces apoptosis in susceptible cells. Selectivity across cancer lines is most plausibly explained by expression of the drug's targets and transporters rather than by any single driver mutation, with ABCC8/KCNJ11 expression and OATP-mediated uptake (SLCO1B1/SLCO2B1) sensitizing cells and efflux/clearance mechanisms protecting them.

features.basis: Encodes SUR1, the primary repaglinide-binding KATP channel subunit; target expression should predict response
Encodes Kir6.2, the pore-forming KATP subunit required for repaglinide-sensitive channel closure
OATP1B1 is a hepatic OATP transporter that mediates uptake of substrate drugs and can increase intracellular exposure
OATP2B1 is a widely expressed OATP influx transporter that can facilitate cellular uptake of anionic drugs
OATP1A2 is expressed in brain and intestinal epithelia and may mediate repaglinide transport in CNS-derived lines
Annotated repaglinide target; PPARG expression may contribute to growth-inhibitory or metabolic effects
P-glycoprotein efflux can lower intracellular repaglinide concentrations and reduce killing
BCRP efflux transporter can limit intracellular accumulation of xenobiotics and protect cells
CYP2C8 metabolizes repaglinide; high expression could reduce active drug exposure in target cells
Glucuronidation inactivates repaglinide and related drugs, lowering effective intracellular concentrations
TP53 mutation is common in the most-killed lines, consistent with impaired DNA-damage/apoptosis checkpoints increasing sensitivity
ARID1A loss appears enriched in sensitive lines and may impair chromatin-based survival responses
